name: Siemens MS41 (BMW M52 / S52)

read_methods.notes: Flashable versions support full reads and programming over the vehicle diagnostic link. The closed-case bench connection uses K-line. Hardware bootstrap recovery uses a direct serial connection inside the case.

notes: Siemens DME for the BMW M52 (MS41.0, MS41.1 OBD-II) and US S52 (MS41.2). OpenTune has no MS4x checksum module yet (checksum null). Pinout from a single source.

bench.notes: ecupinouts: tie +12 V to 26 and 49, ground 28, K-line 88.

safety_note: Bench safety: use a current-limited bench supply (12-13.8 V, start with a low current limit) and a fuse in the +12 V lead; connect ground first. Confirm every pin with a multimeter on YOUR unit before applying power - ground pins should show continuity to each other (and usually the housing), and hardware revisions can differ from the sources. A CAN bus needs about 60 ohm between CAN-H and CAN-L (two 120 ohm terminations): add a 120 ohm resistor if neither the unit nor your interface terminates. Swapped CAN-H/CAN-L just gives timeouts; +12 V on a signal pin can destroy the unit.

obd.notes: Supported versions allow a full 256 KiB read and programming through the vehicle diagnostic socket. Write access requires the vehicle programming-voltage connection. OpenMS41 lists five European MS41.0 versions as non-flashable: 1744598, 1427703, 1744897, 1427704 and 1429999.

bench.how: For closed-case communication, use +12 V on X6000-26 and X6000-49, ground on X6000-28 and K-line on X6000-88. OpenMS41 also identifies X6000-60 as the programming-voltage input for writing.

boot.mcu_mode: SAB 80C166 on-chip bootstrap loader using the ASC0 serial port.

points.name: ALE pull-up
points.note: Pull up to the board’s +5 V rail.

boot.reset_timing: Establish the pull-up and bridge before hardware reset and keep them in place as reset is released. The source gives no subsequent strap-release time.
boot.notes: The recovery project documents these points on its MS41 board and uses a direct full-duplex ASC0 connection inside the case. Coverage across board revisions is unknown.

security.notes: The sources describe full reads, writes and the electrical write-enable connection. They do not establish whether either diagnostic operation requires security access. OpenTune ships no OEM key.
